name: Iceberg REST catalog
shared_by: lakehouse engine source (AWS Glue, Iceberg REST or Unity Catalog)

companions.name: LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES
companions.body:
function run(ctx)
    repeat
        ctx.emit(ctx.files)
    until not ctx.next()
end

inputs.name: catalog_url
inputs.label: Catalog URL (https://host[:port][/path]; http only for this computer or a private network)

inputs.name: namespace
inputs.label: Namespace (one namespace is one virtual schema)

inputs.name: region
inputs.label: Storage region (with an access key: the bucket's region; Enter to let the catalog say)

inputs.name: access_key_id
inputs.label: Storage access key ID (Enter to use a catalog token instead)

access: read on the namespace in the catalog (list and load its tables) and, with storage keys, list and read on the table files (s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject or the store's equivalent)
auth_hint: with --set access_key_id the secret is the storage's secret key; without it, a token the catalog accepts and that lets it vend storage credentials
tips: Names arrive in upper case (ORDERS, ORDER_ID): no quotes needed.
One namespace is one virtual schema: connect again with another --name for the next namespace.
notes: The Glue lakehouse connector's engine over an Iceberg REST catalog: the same pinned lakehouse-engine-rs build, the same LAKEHOUSE_ADAPTER and companion scripts in EXAKIT_VS and the same Rust language container, so a Glue source and a REST source share them.

The CONNECTION goes TO the catalog URL with an empty user; its password is JSON the kit writes: the warehouse plus either storage keys (access_key, secret_key, region and, for MinIO and other S3-compatible stores, endpoint with path-style addressing) or a catalog token with use_vended_credentials, so the catalog hands out short-lived storage credentials per table.

https by default. Plain http is accepted only when typed, and only towards this computer (on macOS 192.168.64.1; on Linux and WSL the address the database sees this computer at - Podman: host.containers.internal; Docker: host.docker.internal where the deployment provides it, else the bridge gateway) or a private network; the virtual schema then carries ALLOW_HTTP = 'true'. localhost is refused: inside the database it is the database itself.
